literal: Broad and refined with military stratagem, he often followed Emperor Taizu on campaigns with merit and was made General of the Martial Guard.
idiomatic: Broad and refined, with real military grasp, he followed Taizu on campaign with merit and was made General of the Martial Guard.

literal: Later he asked leave to retire; Emperor Xianzu treated him with fine courtesy, gave him couch, staff, and robes, and sent meals to his house.
idiomatic: Later he retired; Emperor Xianzu honored him with couch, staff, robes, and meals sent to his house.

literal: He died and was granted secret burial goods.
idiomatic: He died and was granted secret burial goods.

literal: His son Wuzhen had strength beyond other men.
idiomatic: His son Wuzhen had strength beyond other men.

literal: Following Emperor Taizu on campaign he won battle merit again and again and reached Administrator of Julu.
idiomatic: Following Taizu he won repeated battle merit and rose to administrator of Julu.

literal: His son Xingdu was clever, keen, and resolute.
idiomatic: His son Xingdu was clever, keen, and hard.

literal: Under Emperor Gaozong he was Administrator of Hejian and was granted the title Viscount of Lecheng.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he governed Hejian and was made Viscount of Lecheng.

literal: His government was stern and fierce; the common people feared him.
idiomatic: He ruled sternly and the people feared him.

literal: At the start of Emperor Xianzu's reign, because his son Pi was weighty, his rank was advanced to Marquis of Lecheng.
idiomatic: When Xianzu came to the throne, because his son Pi was eminent, he was advanced to Marquis of Lecheng.

literal: He asked leave to retire; Emperor Xianzu honored him still more, gave couch, staff, and robes, and sent meals to his house.
idiomatic: He retired again; Xianzu honored him further with couch, staff, robes, and meals at his house.

literal: His wife, the Lady Lou, was consort-dowager to the Prince of Dongyang.
idiomatic: His wife Lady Lou was consort-dowager to the Prince of Dongyang.

literal: When he died he was posthumously made Regional Inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of Hejian, posthumous title Xuan.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made regional inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of Hejian, posthumous name Xuan.

literal: His son Ti inherited his father's marquisate.
idiomatic: His son Ti inherited the marquisate.

literal: Ti's younger brother Pi was promoted by Emperor Shizu to Gentleman of the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: Ti's younger brother Pi was promoted by Shizu to Gentleman of the Feathered Forest.

literal: Accompanying the emperor to the river campaign, he was granted the title Viscount of Xingping.
idiomatic: On the river campaign he was granted the viscounty of Xingping.

literal: When Emperor Xianzu took the throne he was promoted in succession to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: When Xianzu took the throne he rose in succession to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: When Chancellor Yi Hun plotted rebellion, Pi reported it.
idiomatic: When Chancellor Yi Hun plotted treason, Pi reported it.

literal: An edict ordered Pi to lead Yuan He and Niu Yide to seize Hun and execute him; he was moved to Director of the Masters of Writing and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Dongyang.
idiomatic: An edict had Pi lead Yuan He and Niu Yide to seize and kill Hun; he became Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Dongyang.

literal: Under Emperor Gaozu he was made Prince of Dongyang and Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Works.
idiomatic: Under Gaozu he was made Prince of Dongyang, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Duke of Works.

literal: At that time there were more than three hundred doubtful matters; an edict ordered Pi to decide them; on the whole his judgments were fair.
idiomatic: More than three hundred doubtful cases were sent to him to decide; his judgments were mostly fair.

literal: When Pi's son Chao was born the imperial carriage personally visited his house with special rewards.
idiomatic: When Pi's son Chao was born the emperor visited his house with special gifts.

literal: Because his loyalty was undivided, an edict granted Pi entry into the Eight Pardons, to be transmitted to his descendants; for crimes up to a hundred lashes he might be rebuked and forgiven;
idiomatic: For undivided loyalty an edict granted Pi the Eight Pardons for his line: crimes up to a hundred lashes might be rebuked and forgiven;

literal: the corvée and tax labor of males of his registered household were released forever;
idiomatic: males of his household were forever freed from corvée and tax labor;

literal: [11] if any wicked man should conveniently slander him, that man was to be beheaded at once.
idiomatic: [11] anyone who slandered him by trickery was to be beheaded at once.

literal: Soon he was moved to Grand Commandant and Recorder of Masters of Writing Affairs.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Commandant and recorder of Masters of Writing affairs.

literal: At that time Prince of Huainan Ta, Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan, and Prince of Hedong Gou Ti were all honored as elders of former times; whenever great affairs arose they were brought into the forbidden precinct, rode in hand-drawn carriages, and leaned on staffs at court, advancing and withdrawing together.
idiomatic: Prince of Huainan Ta, Prince of Huaiyang Wei Yuan, and Prince of Hedong Gou Ti were honored as elders; on great affairs they entered the palace in hand-drawn carriages with staffs at court, moving together.

literal: Pi, Ta, and Yuan—the three of them—were all of imposing build, belts ten spans round, large ears and fine brows, beards and temples grizzled; the hundred offices looked on and none failed to stand in awe.
idiomatic: Pi, Ta, and Yuan were imposing men—belts ten spans round, large ears, fine brows, grizzled beards; officials looked on in awe.

literal: Only Gou Ti was somewhat shorter and smaller; his bearing and looks did not reach theirs.
idiomatic: Only Gou Ti was shorter; his looks did not match.

literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming valued age and honored the old; they sent frequent inquiries and thick gifts of treasures.
idiomatic: Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming honored age with frequent visits and rich gifts.

literal: Pi's voice was high and clear; he remembered state affairs broadly; at banquets he always sat at the head and would raise his voice to speak at length, recounting past success and failure.
idiomatic: Pi spoke in a high, clear voice and remembered state affairs; at banquets he sat at the head and recounted past victories and defeats in a ringing voice.

literal: The emperor and empress listened with respect.
idiomatic: The emperor and empress listened with respect.

literal: Yet he flattered those in power and was arrogant toward the lowly; whenever he saw Wang Rui or Fu Chengzu he would bend his body to place himself below them.
idiomatic: Yet he flattered the powerful and despised the lowly; before Wang Rui or Fu Chengzu he bent low.

literal: At that time Empress Dowager Wenming built a mansion for Wang Rui, so she also built a first-rank mansion for Pi.
idiomatic: Wenming built a mansion for Wang Rui and likewise a first-rank house for Pi.

literal: When the house was finished the emperor and empress visited in person and led the hundred civil and military officials to a housewarming feast.
idiomatic: When it was finished the emperor and empress visited and feasted the civil and military officials there.

literal: Wang Rui, Director of the Masters of Writing, was ordered to proclaim the edict and grant Pi one golden seal-cord.
idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Rui proclaimed an edict granting Pi one golden seal-cord.

literal: The empress dowager personally composed admonitory song-verses and gave them to the officials; Pi submitted a memorial of praise and thanks.
idiomatic: The empress dowager composed admonitory songs for the officials; Pi thanked her in a memorial.

literal: The empress dowager ordered, "Ministers, neighbors! Neighbors, ministers!
idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Ministers, neighbors! Neighbors, ministers!

literal: The ruler must not idle above; ministers must walk on ice below.
idiomatic: The ruler must not idle above; ministers must walk on ice below.

literal: If you can be thus, how hard is great peace to attain?"
idiomatic: If you can be thus, how hard is peace to win?"

literal: When Pi's wife the Lady Duan died she was given the posthumous title Consort Gong.
idiomatic: When Pi's wife Lady Duan died she received the posthumous title Consort Gong.

literal: Pi was also specially granted a golden tally.
idiomatic: Pi was also specially granted a golden tally.

literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming received the dukes and ministers in the Hall of Imperial Trust and the empress dowager said, "Now the capital suffers drought and dearth; I wish to let hungry and poor people leave the passes to seek food elsewhere.
idiomatic: Gaozu and Wenming received the ministers in the Hall of Imperial Trust; the empress dowager said, "The capital suffers drought and dearth; I wish to let the hungry poor leave the passes to seek food.

literal: If we issue travel permits I fear days will be lost and the disaster will not be relieved; if we let them go freely I again fear good and wicked will be hard to tell apart.
idiomatic: Travel permits may cost days we do not have; free departure may mix honest folk with rogues.

literal: You should debate what is fitting."
idiomatic: Debate what is fitting."

literal: Pi argued, "Every gentleman of the Masters of Writing from junior clerk upward should each take two clerks and separately manage issuing permits; commanderies and counties likewise—within three days at most issuance would be finished; what difficulty is there?"
idiomatic: Pi said: "Let every Masters of Writing gentleman from junior clerk up take two clerks each to issue permits; let commanderies and counties do the same—in three days it would be done. What difficulty?"

literal: Emperor Gaozu followed this; in four days it was finished.
idiomatic: Gaozu agreed; in four days it was finished.

literal: Pi asked to establish the Eastern Palace; the edict said, "The years are still young—what hurry is there?"
idiomatic: Pi asked to establish the crown prince; the edict answered, "He is still young—what hurry?"

literal: Pi said, "Your servant's years stand in the western dusk; I long to witness the great rite—for me it is urgent."
idiomatic: Pi said, "My years stand in the western dusk; I long to see the great rite—for me it is urgent."

literal: He was not permitted.
idiomatic: Permission was refused.

literal: Later, by precedent, princely rank was reduced; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang commandery.
idiomatic: Later, by precedent, his princely rank was reduced to Duke of Pingyang commandery.

literal: He asked to resign office; the edict did not permit it.
idiomatic: He asked to resign; the edict refused.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Pi and Prince of Guangling Yu remained to guard the capital, both given credential-bearing authority.
idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Pi and Prince of Guangling Yu guarded the capital, both with credential-bearing authority.

literal: The edict to Pi and Yu said, "To remain and guard, none but the worthy will do.
idiomatic: The edict to Pi and Yu said, "Only the worthy can guard the capital.

literal: The Grand Commandant is advanced in years and heavy in virtue; his post sums up the regent's charge;
idiomatic: The Grand Commandant is old and weighty in virtue, his post the pivot of government;

literal: Yu is Our splendid younger brother, gentle, warm, clear, and decisive.
idiomatic: Yu is Our splendid younger brother—gentle, warm, clear, and decisive.

literal: Therefore We send these two to guard the capital city and grant them two credentials with reward and punishment in hand.
idiomatic: We send these two to guard the capital with two credentials and reward and punishment in hand.

literal: Reverently fulfill the established statutes to match Our heart."
idiomatic: Fulfill the statutes faithfully to match Our heart."

literal: Pi replied, "I respectfully obey unto death."
idiomatic: Pi answered, "I will obey unto death."

literal: Yu replied, "The Grand Commandant should hold sole command; your servant can only be second."
idiomatic: Yu answered, "The Grand Commandant should command alone; I can only assist."

literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "The old have wisdom; the young have decision—how can you decline?"
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The old have wisdom, the young decision—how can you decline?"

literal: When Emperor Gaozu returned to Dai, Pi asked to compose a song; the edict permitted it.
idiomatic: When Gaozu returned to Dai, Pi asked to compose a song and was permitted.

literal: When the song was finished Emperor Gaozu said, "You inclined Our returning carriage, so We personally sang to state Our intent.
idiomatic: When the song was done Gaozu said, "You bent Our returning carriage, so We sang Our intent in person.

literal: Now construction already has its order; We therefore return for a time to the old capital—may later times share this joy as well."
idiomatic: Construction has its order; We return for a time to the old capital—may later days share this joy."

literal: When Emperor Gaozu wished to move the capital he came to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, summoned the remaining guard officers, and held great debate.
idiomatic: When Gaozu wished to move the capital he came to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, summoned the guard officers, and held great debate.

literal: He then ordered Pi and the others that if they had thoughts they should each state their will.
idiomatic: He ordered Pi and the others each to speak his mind.

literal: Regional Inspector of Yanzhou Mu Ba advanced and said, "The matter of moving the capital is great; in this servant's foolish view it cannot yet be done."
idiomatic: Regional Inspector of Yanzhou Mu Ba said, "Moving the capital is great; in my foolish view it cannot yet be done."

literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Then speak the reasons it cannot be done."
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Speak the reasons it cannot be done."

literal: Ba said, "In the north are the Xianyun raiders; in the south Jing and Yang are not yet submitted; in the west Tuyuhun blocks the way; in the east Koguryo is hard to overcome.
idiomatic: Ba said, "North are Xianyun raiders; south Jing and Yang are unsubmitted; west Tuyuhun blocks; east Koguryo is hard.

literal: The four quarters are not yet pacified; the nine regions are not yet settled.
idiomatic: The four quarters are not pacified; the nine regions unsettled.

literal: From this I infer it cannot be done."
idiomatic: From this I infer it cannot be done."

literal: Campaigns require war-horses; without horses affairs cannot succeed."
idiomatic: Campaigns need war-horses; without horses nothing succeeds."

literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Your saying there are no horses is roughly acceptable.
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Your point about horses is roughly acceptable.

literal: Horses always come from the north; the stud is placed here—why worry there will be no horses?
idiomatic: Horses come from the north; the stud is here—why fear there will be none?

literal: Now Dai lies north of Mount Heng, outside the Nine Provinces; for this reason We move to the central plain."
idiomatic: Dai lies north of Mount Heng, outside the Nine Provinces; for that We move to the central plain."

literal: Ba said, "I have heard that the Yellow Emperor's capital was at Zhuolu.
idiomatic: Ba said, "I hear the Yellow Emperor's capital was Zhuolu.

literal: From this, ancient sage kings did not all dwell in the central plain."
idiomatic: So ancient sage kings did not all dwell in the central plain."

literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "The Yellow Emperor, because the realm was not settled, dwelt at Zhuolu; once it was settled he also moved to Henan."
idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The Yellow Emperor dwelt at Zhuolu while the realm was unsettled; once settled he moved to Henan."

literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Guo said: [12] "Your servant truly does not know ancient affairs; as I hear the common people speak, the late emperor built the capital here—suddenly to move, they think it cannot be done.
idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Guo said: [12] "I truly do not know antiquity; as the people say, the late emperor built here—to move suddenly they think cannot be done.

literal: The central plain is as they describe for the reasons they imagine.
idiomatic: The central plain is what they imagine it to be.

literal: [13] There have been many usurpations.
idiomatic: [13] There have been many usurpations.

literal: Since the founding of the city at Pingcheng it has been firm as heaven and earth, bright as sun and moon.
idiomatic: Since Pingcheng was founded it has stood firm as heaven and earth, bright as sun and moon.

literal: Your servant's shallow tube-view and nature not bright and penetrating would never compare the land of Heng and Dai to the beauty of Yiluo.
idiomatic: My shallow sight would never compare Heng and Dai to the beauty of Yiluo.

literal: But settling on the soil and honoring migration are the constant nature of things; once moved south in a day, I fear they will not be glad."
idiomatic: Yet honoring the soil and dreading migration are human nature; move south in a day and I fear they will not rejoice."

literal: Pi said, "Your Majesty last year personally led the Six Armies to punish the Xiao clan and reached Luoyang; Prince of Renyang Cheng proclaimed the intent and ordered your servants to debate moving the capital to Luo.
idiomatic: Pi said, "Last year Your Majesty led the Six Armies against the Xiao house to Luoyang; Prince of Renyang Cheng ordered us to debate moving the capital to Luo.

literal: When I first received the gracious command my heart was anxious and unsettled.
idiomatic: When I first received the command my heart was anxious.

literal: Whenever one wishes to migrate one should consult divination by milfoil and tortoise and determine fortune or ill fortune—only then may one act."
idiomatic: Any migration should ask the milfoil and tortoise and fix fortune or ill fortune—only then act."

literal: Emperor Gaozu said to Pi, "Formerly at Ye, Duke of Works Dan, Prince of Xianyang Xi, and Director of the Masters of Writing Li Chong all wished to request tortoise divination for the fortune of moving to Luo.
idiomatic: Gaozu said to Pi, "At Ye, Dan Duke of Works, Xi Prince of Xianyang, and Li Chong all wished to divine moving to Luo.

literal: I then told Dan and the others that in antiquity the Duke of Zhou divined the site at Yiluo and so knew the utmost omen.
idiomatic: I told them that in antiquity the Duke of Zhou divined Yiluo and knew the utmost omen.

literal: Now there is no one like him; divination is also of no use.
idiomatic: Now there is no one like him; divination is useless.

literal: Yet divination exists to resolve doubt; here there is no doubt—why need divination?
idiomatic: Divination resolves doubt; here there is no doubt—why divine?

literal: Formerly when Xuanyuan divined, the tortoise scorched; the diviner asked to consult the worthy; Xuanyuan then asked Tian Lao, and Tian Lao said it was good.
idiomatic: When Xuanyuan divined, the tortoise scorched; the diviner asked the wise; Xuanyuan asked Tian Lao, who said it was good.

literal: He followed that word and in the end attained prosperity and good fortune.
idiomatic: He followed that and attained prosperity.

literal: Thus the utmost man's measure is not yet settled, but is clearer than the tortoise.
idiomatic: The utmost man's measure is not yet settled, yet clearer than tortoise shells.

literal: I have already taken the four seas as home; south or north, slow or fast—there is no fixed rule.
idiomatic: I have made the four seas my home; south or north, slow or fast—no fixed rule.

literal: For the people who move south I myself will pile storehouses high so they will not suffer want."
idiomatic: For those who move south I will pile storehouses so they do not suffer want."

literal: Pi said, "Your servant respectfully received the gracious command and cannot contain joy and dance."
idiomatic: Pi said, "I received the gracious command and cannot contain my joy."

literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered the officials, "Some of you perhaps think I have no intent to move.
idiomatic: Gaozu told the officials, "Some of you think I will not move.

literal: Formerly Emperor Pingwen abandoned his back to the realm; Emperor Zhaocheng built his dwelling at Shengle;
idiomatic: Emperor Pingwen turned his back on the realm; Emperor Zhaocheng built at Shengle;

literal: Emperor Taizu Daowu by divine martiality answered Heaven and moved his dwelling to Pingcheng.
idiomatic: Taizu Daowu by divine martiality answered Heaven and moved to Pingcheng.

literal: I, though empty and few, have the good fortune to belong to an age that conquers the cruel; therefore I move my house to the central plain and begin the imperial realm.
idiomatic: I, though empty and few, have fortune in an age that conquers the cruel; therefore I move to the central plain and begin the imperial realm.
